etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English sinceritie, from Old French sincerité and Medieval Latin sincēritas; both from Latin sincēritas, from sincērus + -tās. Equivalent to sincere +‎ -ity.

definitions.definition: The quality or state of being sincere.

quote.citation: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Othello, the Moore of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene iii]:
quote.text: I protest, in the sincerity of love.

quote.citation: c. 1779-1790, Vicesimus Knox, Essays Moral and Literary:
quote.text: If the shew of any thing be good for any thing, I am sure sincerity is better
